I'll start by naming the session and unpacking the archive.The `edit` tool stripped the trailing spaces. I'll use a shell command instead, which preserves them.Trailing spaces are in place. Let me verify the Markdown actually renders as separate lines.No renderer is installed, so I'll verify byte-level correctness instead: strip the two added spaces and confirm the result matches the original file exactly (proving nothing else changed).Done.
**What I changed:** `README.md` — added two trailing spaces to the first two lines under `## Contact`:
```
Payments Team··
Building 4, Floor 2··
payments@example.com
```
(`·` = space; the third line is untouched, since it's the last line and needs no break)
**Verification:**
- `cat -A` confirms both lines end with exactly two spaces before the newline (lines 7 and 8).
- No blank lines were inserted, and the third contact line and the rest of the file are byte-identical to the original (verified by stripping the two added space pairs and diffing against the original content — identical).
One note: the `edit` tool silently strips trailing whitespace, so this had to be applied via `perl -i -pe`. If you make future edits to these lines with an editor that trims whitespace, the hard breaks will be lost. No Markdown renderer (`pandoc`/`cmark`/`node`) was available in the sandbox, so I couldn't produce a rendered HTML check — but two-plus trailing spaces is the CommonMark hard-break rule GitHub uses.
